1101-winter-term: PHYS 142 is an alternative; CHEM 212 can be taken intensively in May. Also Casper and French.
Inter-faculty transfers: form on Minerva from March 1, Casper and French, all by April 1; incomplete or late files may be invalid. See p. 39.

You enter as U1. Up to 30 transfer credits, requested in your first term and processed by December; they must match McGill's in content and evaluation without overlaps. Courses are set by year, with no mixing, so the degree takes exactly three years. No switching between OT and PT; apply to the other's Qualifying Year in your final year.
1101-admission-requirements-for-qualifyi: With a degree other than McGill's OT or PT B.Sc., complete a Qualifying Year first, applying through Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies. See SPOT's Admissions page.
1101-program-description: Health sciences for OT: occupation in daily life, community rehabilitation, client-centred and evidence-based practice, reasoning, ethics, teamwork and professionalism.
1102-complementary-courses-15-credits: Before U3, from Psychology, Management (personnel, private practice), Academic Writing, Sociology or Anthropology, French or English second language if needed (up to 6). Also a 3-credit Sports Medicine Practicum, by interview, and up to 3 of personal interest.
1102-program-description: Health sciences for PT: reasoning, diagnostics, evidence-based practice, community rehabilitation, teamwork and professionalism.
1103-complementary-courses-6-9-credits: Before U3, from Psychology, Management (personnel, private practice), Academic Writing, Sociology or Anthropology, and French or English second language if needed (up to 6).
1104-about-the-faculty-of-science: Professors and students work together, from cognitive science to cosmology, and you can join their research. Fifteen departments offer the B.Sc., with fieldwork, research projects, internships and cross-disciplinary work.
1104-mcgill-s-faculty-of-science: McGill's second-largest faculty: nine schools and departments, five affiliated, multi-department programs and a dozen-plus research centres. 5,000+ undergraduates, 1,000+ graduates and 260+ faculty. Ten Nobel laureates in its history: seven alumni, three faculty or staff.
Leading in Canada on astrophysics, climate, green chemistry, developmental biology, earth systems, biodiversity, nanoscience, social neuroscience, sustainability and AI.

Field study in East Africa, Barbados and Panama; Fessenden Professorships and Prizes for commercializing research; the $120 million Life Sciences Research Complex; Canada's first comprehensive Earth System Science Program; the Office of Science Education; Science Undergraduate Research Awards.
1104-programs-and-teaching-in-science: Leading researchers teach undergraduates, and independent study lets you contribute. All B.Sc. programs can include an internship, with Work Study and research jobs too. Admission is selective.

Two diplomas, all credits at McGill: Environment (30 credits, p. 870) for B.Sc. or B.A. holders, and Meteorology (30 credits, p. 1134), one year for math, engineering, physics and similar graduates. The B.A. & Sc. is joint with Arts (p. 428).
1104-academic-units: Units offering B.Sc. courses; some, such as Pathology, belong to other faculties. See p. 1107 for structuring your degree.
1105-prospective-high-school-cegep-and-u: McGill's Admissions Office reviews files. You pick a Program Group when applying, which sets your program range and maybe requirements. Changing needs a competitive Intrafaculty Transfer after a year.
1105-degree-advising-and-sousa: SOUSA houses degree advisors for the B.Sc. and B.A. & Sc., helping with planning, study away, readmission, transfers and hard times. Your advisor is named on your Unofficial Transcript; advisor.science@mcgill.ca.

Ask about Foundation, planning, requirements, rules, exchange, deferring exams, transfers and readmission. Write to the Associate Dean, Student Affairs for special requests; the Committee on Student Standing hears appeals.
1106-first-year-advising: See Science's new student site. The B.Sc. is 120 credits with a mandatory Foundation Program (p. 1111); Advanced Standing from CEGEP, IB, A-Levels, AP or French Baccalaureate may exempt you, but you must still check you meet it.
U0 (97–120 credits needed): register for Foundation courses, with SOUSA's advice. U1 (96 or fewer): declare your program at registration, consulting a program advisor and your degree advisor.
1106-degree-requirements-for-the-faculty: Advisors help, but you are responsible for courses, requirements and deadlines. Misunderstanding is no excuse.
1106-bachelor-of-arts-and-science-b-a-sc: Joint with Arts (p. 150), with advising through SOUSA and Science's Associate Dean. See p. 430.
1106-diploma-dip-in-environment: One year full-time for graduates reorienting. 30 credits at McGill; C or better in required and complementary courses.
1106-diploma-dip-in-meteorology: An intensive year of theory and applied work for B.Sc. or B.Eng. graduates in physics, applied math or similar. 30 credits at McGill; C or better.
1107-b-sc-m-sc-track: Early admission for strong McGill undergraduates into a Science M.Sc. or M.A.
1107-program-requirements: 120 credits. Your Program Group limits your choices. Do the Foundation Program, or get exempted through Advanced Standing or Placement Exams (p. 1111). Then, usually at the start of U1, pick a structure (Liberal, Major, Honours or Joint) and specific programs.
1107-course-requirements-for-bachelor-of: C or better in required and complementary courses, including basic science. If you fail: pass a supplemental, do extra work if allowed, or repeat. Substitutions only in special cases.

Normally one repeat; failure means below C, or J or KF. A third try needs the Associate Dean's permission by email through your advisor; if denied there and on appeal to the Committee, you must withdraw. Failed complementaries can be replaced, with a D kept as an elective credit. A repeated required D gives credit once.
1107-course-overlap: No extra credit for content overlapping McGill, CEGEP, other university, AP, A Level, IB or French Baccalaureate work. Check exclusions with SOUSA or the department.
Double-prefix courses like LING 345 / COMP 345: take your own department's version if offered at once; otherwise whichever fits.

Statistics and computing from other faculties need the Associate Dean's permission (computing only exceptionally); Environment majors may take required statistics in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Arts students: computer course credit follows each course description.

Statistics: credit for only one listed introductory course; PSYC 204 blocks the list; only one intermediate course, except PSYC 305 with ECON 227D1/D2 or 257D1/D2; MATH 324 or 357 blocks the list. For other 500-level statistics, ask an advisor about overlap.
1108-courses-outside-the-faculties-of-ar: 6 credits a year, 18 in total, with prerequisites and the instructor's permission. See the Undergraduate Handbook, 3.2.2, for approved and restricted courses: restricted never count; others need the Associate Dean's approval by email to your advisor. Minerva may let you in, but excess or unapproved courses get flagged for no credit.

BIOT, EXMD and PHAR count as Science. Music is outside, except MUAR. RELG counts, except B.Th. or S.T.M. courses and those needing the Chair's permission. No credit for "how to" courses, such as software, SQL or COBOL, shop, drawing or professional practice. Outside computing and statistics only exceptionally.

May exceed 18 if needed for the program: Bieler School students, Software Engineering majors, and Liberal students in a Music Major Concentration (up to 36). The limit applies to the Nutrition Minor; take Science equivalents.
1109-correspondence-distance-education-o: Transfer credit needs prior approval from the department for content and SOUSA for delivery (Handbook 4.5). Outside courses must come from an accredited degree-granting school, count there, and fit within credit limits. They can't meet program requirements, except for serious documented reasons.
1109-courses-in-english-as-a-second-lang: For those whose first language isn't English, with under five years in English secondary school. Up to 12 credits, including academic writing.
1109-first-year-seminars-registration-fo: For new U0 or U1 students, first-come, 25 at most: closer contact with professors, and current research methods. Only one.
1109-first-year-seminars: Arts seminars are open to Science students (p. 167).
1109-course-credit-weight: One credit is about 45 hours of class, lab and personal study.
1110-advanced-standing: 120 credits normally; up to 30 granted for DEC, IB, French Baccalaureate, A Levels, AP (declare scores of 4 or 5 at first registration), or college courses counted toward a diploma. A Science DCS normally exempts you from basic sciences; others may be too.
No credit for overlaps with past credit or exemptions. You may still choose to do 120 McGill credits, within repeat limits.
1110-equivalencies-for-non-basic-science: CHEM 212, CHEM 222, PSYC 204 and others vary by CEGEP, and may need a higher grade. See the Transfer Credit site or your SOUSA advisor.
1110-residency-requirement-for-the-b-sc: 60 credits at McGill, excluding Foundation, and normally two-thirds of departmental requirements, not counting a prior McGill degree. Study Away or Exchange can be exempted with department and Associate Dean approval; some departments have other rules. Diplomas: 30 credits.
1110-time-and-credit-limit-for-the-compl: With 96 or fewer credits to do: eight terms at most; Foundation students a year after first registering. Finish within 120 credits; you get credit up to the term you reach it. Going past either limit needs the Associate Dean's approval by email, for reasons like program change or part-time, then only required and complementary courses count. Those with Advanced Standing from IB, AP, A-Levels and similar may do 120 after admission (p. 55).
1111-overview-of-programs-offered: Foundation (p. 1111); Liberal, Major, Honours and Joint by Program Group (p. 1112); Arts programs open to Science students (p. 1114). See p. 1107.
1111-science-foundation-program: 30 credits of basic science before your three-year program; Advanced Standing may exempt you. U0 students take these in first year; U1 students declare a program, with program and degree advisors.
1111-program-description: For those needing 97–120 credits; SOUSA must approve courses (newstudentadvising.science@mcgill.ca). 30 credits, including at least seven Approved Foundation Year Science courses.
1111-general-math-and-science-breadth: Six courses: 2 MATH and 4 of BIOL, CHEM or PHYS; or 3 MATH and 3 of BIOL, CHEM or PHYS.
1111-science-complementary: A seventh from the list. Missing grade 12 biology, chemistry or physics? Take one. Many take more to keep majors open; check department rules. Five courses a term at most. Some medical and dental schools have set requirements.
1112-list-of-approved-foundation-year-sc: Choose as instructed. CHEM 120 isn't open after CHEM 115. One each of first and second calculus, and first and second physics.
1112-electives: Introductory Science or Arts courses; see the recommended list. Some other faculties' courses are allowed, with limits.
1112-bachelor-of-science-programs-by-pro: Your Program Group, chosen when applying, sets your range. Changing is a competitive Intra-Faculty Transfer after a year.
1113-joint-programs: None in the Biological, Biomedical, Life Sciences Group.
1114-science-minor-programs: Includes Management for Non-Management Students. Chemical Engineering is only for Chemistry students, Electrical Engineering only for Physics majors, and General Science only for Liberal students.
1115-minor-concentrations: Includes Quebec Studies and Community-Engaged Learning (18 credits, p. 277).
1116-undergraduate-research-opportunitie: Most B.Sc. students do research, at McGill, hospitals, other universities or in the field. See awards like USRA and SURA, the Dean's Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research List, and Internships and Field Studies (p. 1117).
1116-getting-involved-in-research-as-an-: Voluntary, for credit or paid; some are formal programs, others come from talking with professors. The Science site has tips.
1116-beyond-mcgill: Try foundations, agencies, hospitals, other universities or scholarly societies, including in other countries.
1116-research-project-courses: Supervised research for credit, under names like majors or honours project, advanced lab or independent study. They can help toward the Dean's Research List or B.Sc. Global Designation.
1116-396-undergraduate-research-project-: Offered by all Science units, such as ANAT, ATOC, BIOC and BIOL 396, plus COGS, ENVR, HGEN, MDPH, NSCI, PATH and BASC 396, and FSCI 396, 397 and 398D1/D2. Electives, generally after a term, even outside your department, approved by supervisor and department.
1116-undergraduate-science-showcase: A yearly event where students present research and projects, open to the community.
1117-undergraduate-student-research-awar: Fund projects, usually in summer, at McGill and sometimes elsewhere.
1117-tri-agency-undergraduate-student-re: Funded by NSERC, CIHR and SSHRC, for paid supervised research that encourages graduate study. For Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons.
1117-sura-science-undergraduate-research: Since summer 2007, like USRA but open to international students too: full-time supervised research, funded by donors, supervisors and the Faculty.
1117-science-field-studies-and-internshi: Coordinates field semesters for all undergraduates, and internships for Science and B.A. & Sc. students, plus Arts students in Environment, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Geography, Math and Psychology. By appointment: 2001 McGill College, 646B.
1117-internship-program-industrial-pract: Industrial Practicum (4 months) for those groups; Internship Year (8, 12 or 16 months) for Science only. Requires full-time status beforehand, 27+ credits done, 12+ left, and CGPA 2.7. International students have restrictions. Two practica or an Internship Year add "Internship Program" to your Science degree name.
1117-field-study-semester-programs: Research-based 15-credit semesters in East Africa, Barbados and Panama, plus shorter courses in Biology, Earth and Planetary Sciences, and Geography.
1118-b-sc-global-designation: Internships and study abroad can earn this at graduation.
1118-summer-studies-in-the-faculty-of-sc: Special summer courses; see Minerva for all.
1118-earth-and-planetary-sciences: Off-campus field courses. Confirm with the instructor by January 31 for EPSC 231 and December 31 for EPSC 331 and 341; no late registrants, and withdrawals need a documented reason. EPSC 240 students may join 231 by requesting a permit.
1118-examinations: See p. 62; applies up to 500 level. Tentative schedules come a month after classes start, and final ones after two. Don't plan to leave before exams end.
1119-browse-academic-units-and-programs: Approved for 2026–27; some units belong to other faculties. See p. 1107, and p. 1111 if you're from outside Quebec.
1120-about-anatomy-and-cell-biology: Cell biology, histology, embryology, neuroanatomy and gross anatomy. Honours starts careers in cell and molecular biology; Major and Liberal are broader. Good for graduate study, medicine, and lab or administrative jobs.
Labs for protein purification, recombinant DNA, micro-injection, microscopy, proteomics and genomics, a unique cryo-electron microscope, a cadaver lab and 3D printers.
1120-location: Strathcona Anatomy and Dentistry Building, Rooms M21–M31, 3640 University St., H3A 0C7.
